enzyme_name: Monolignol 4-O-beta-glucosidase (coniferin beta-glucosidase family, glycoside hydrolase family 1)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana BGLU45/BGLU46; Pinus contorta coniferin beta-glucosidase (lignifying xylem)
rationale: Recombinant Arabidopsis BGLU45 and BGLU46 were purified to homogeneity and shown to hydrolyse p-coumaryl alcohol 4-O-glucoside and the other monolignol glucosides; these are single-domain GH1 retaining beta-glucosidases with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: A GH1 beta-glucosidase runs hydrolytically (glucoside + H2O -> glucose + p-coumaryl alcohol, left-to-right as written); the glucoside is made by a UDP-glucose:monolignol glucosyltransferase, not by reversal of this enzyme, so ModelSEED's '<' (condensation releasing water) has no enzymatic basis and the LLM's '>' matches the enzymology.

organism_context: Nocardia sp. strain P18.3 (native enzyme ~50 kDa, two dissimilar subunits of 17 and 22 kDa); Pseudomonas rhodesiae CIP 107491 Pra-POL, a single 202-residue, 23.7 kDa NTF2-superfamily polypeptide
rationale: The Nocardia enzyme was purified to homogeneity as a cofactor-free protein catalysing a single concerted epoxide-opening/decyclization, and the cloned P. rhodesiae gene encodes one short polypeptide with that same single activity; no second catalytic function is reported.
direction_note: Catalysis proceeds through a reactive carbocation and even inactivates the enzyme during turnover, so it is effectively irreversible in the ring-opening direction (alpha-pinene oxide -> isonovalal, left-to-right as written); recyclization of the acyclic dienal, which ModelSEED's '<' requires, is not an activity of this lyase.

enzyme_name: unassigned (no enzyme is known for FAD-dependent Delta4 desaturation of 3-dehydrosphinganine)
rationale: KEGG R04092 carries no EC number, no KO and no pathway assignment, and no protein has been reported that desaturates 3-dehydrosphinganine (3-ketosphinganine) to 3-ketosphingosine; the characterised sphingolipid Delta4 desaturase (DEGS1/DES1) acts on dihydroceramide, not on the free 3-keto long-chain base, so this is a legacy route with no catalyst.
direction_note: If the step existed, biosynthetic flux would be desaturation (3-dehydrosphinganine -> 3-ketosphingosine, left-to-right as written); nothing supports ModelSEED's '<', i.e. FADH2-driven reduction of the Delta4 bond, but with no identified enzyme neither call rests on enzymology.

organism_context: Human/mammalian mitochondrial IVD (leucine catabolism); bacterial LiuA; plant IVD
rationale: IVD is a homotetrameric mitochondrial FAD enzyme of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family with a single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation activity; its electron acceptor ETF is a separate two-subunit protein, which under the protocol's complex exclusion does not make IVD bifunctional.
direction_note: ACAD-family dehydrogenation is drained to ETF/ETF-QO and runs only toward the enoyl-CoA (isovaleryl-CoA -> 3-methylcrotonyl/dimethylacryloyl-CoA, left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would run leucine catabolism backwards, a reduction that belongs to a different (enoyl-CoA reductase) enzyme.

organism_context: Escherichia coli and Kluyvera citrophila periplasmic alpha/beta heterodimer matured from a single pac precursor
rationale: PGA has one catalytic activity, hydrolysis of the phenylacetyl amide bond of penicillin G; the alpha/beta heterodimer arises by Ntn-hydrolase autoproteolytic self-maturation of one precursor chain, which is self-processing rather than a second metabolic activity, and a circularly permuted single-chain variant is fully active.
direction_note: The equilibrium lies far toward hydrolysis (penicillin G + H2O -> phenylacetate + 6-APA, left-to-right as written); industrial penicillin synthesis with PGA is kinetically controlled from activated acyl donors (esters/amides), not thermodynamic reversal, so ModelSEED's '<' does not correspond to how the enzyme works.

enzyme_name: Aryl sulfotransferase IV / tyrosine-ester sulfotransferase (rat SULT1A1)
organism_context: Rattus norvegicus liver cytosol; expressed as a single recombinant polypeptide
rationale: AST IV was purified from rat liver cytosol and bacterially expressed as one polypeptide with a single activity, PAPS-dependent O-sulfonation of phenolic and tyrosine-ester acceptors; its reaction-product self-inactivation by N-hydroxy-2-acetylaminofluorene sulfate is enzyme inactivation, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is strongly exergonic and effectively irreversible toward the sulfated product (PAPS + L-tyrosine methyl ester -> PAP + the 4-sulfate, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' reverses a committed transfer step; the LLM's '>' matches the enzymology.

organism_context: Synechocystis PCC6803 ChlM; Rhodobacter capsulatus BchM; Arabidopsis and rice CHLM
rationale: ChlM is a small class-I (seven-stranded beta-sheet) SAM-dependent methyltransferase with one activity, methyl esterification of the C13 propionate of Mg-protoporphyrin IX; its physical association with Mg-chelatase subunits is a protein-protein interaction and its role in plastid-to-nucleus signalling is regulatory moonlighting, neither of which counts as a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible in the methylation direction (SAM + Mg-proto IX -> SAH + Mg-proto IX monomethyl ester, left-to-right as written) and commits the porphyrin to the chlorophyll branch, so ModelSEED's '<' is not physiological.

enzyme_name: unassigned (KEGG R04252 is explicitly flagged 'incomplete reaction')
rationale: KEGG R04252 (2-aminoethylphosphonate/ciliatine <=> ciliatocholate) carries no EC number, no KO and no enzyme assignment and is annotated 'incomplete reaction'; ciliatocholate is the 2-aminoethylphosphonate conjugate of cholic acid first described in bovine bile, so the real chemistry is bile-acid (de)conjugation, but no protein has ever been assigned to it.
direction_note: As written the reaction is mass-unbalanced (the cholate moiety is simply dropped), so both the thermodynamic estimates and the direction calls are meaningless; read as bile-acid deconjugation, hydrolysis releasing free ciliatine would be the favoured direction, which is ModelSEED's '<' rather than the LLM's '>'.

organism_context: Pseudomonas, acyclic terpene (citronellol/geraniol) degradation
rationale: Seubert and Fass purified this lyase from Pseudomonas separately from the preceding beta-isohexenylglutaconyl-CoA hydratase, showing the hydratase and lyase steps sit on distinct proteins rather than a fused bifunctional chain; only the acetate-releasing retro-aldol activity was found on the lyase. The protein has not been cloned, hence medium rather than high confidence.
direction_note: In citronellol/geraniol catabolism this lyase runs in the cleavage direction (3-hydroxy-3-isohexenylglutaryl-CoA -> acetate + 7-methyl-3-oxooctanoyl-CoA, left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would require a C-C condensation that the degradative pathway never performs, so the LLM's '>' is correct.

enzyme_name: Aerobactin synthetases IucA and IucC (NIS synthetases)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae iuc operon
rationale: The lumped EC 6.3.2.27 'aerobactin synthase' reaction is not one enzyme: two separate NRPS-independent siderophore (NIS) synthetases, IucA and IucC, sequentially couple N6-acetyl-N6-hydroxylysine to the two carboxylates of citrate, each a distinct polypeptide performing one ATP-dependent adenylation/amidation; neither carries a second fused activity.
direction_note: Each condensation is driven by ATP cleavage and is irreversible toward aerobactin (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would amount to regenerating 4 ATP by hydrolysing the siderophore, which is thermodynamically impossible, so the LLM's '>' is correct.

organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Candida Erg6p; plant, Mucor and protist SMT orthologues
rationale: Erg6p is a single-domain SAM-dependent C-methyltransferase whose only activity is C-24 methylation of zymosterol to fecosterol; organisms that need more than one SMT activity duplicate the gene (e.g. the multiple SMTs of Mucor lusitanicus) rather than fusing extra catalytic domains.
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-alkylation via a high-energy carbocation intermediate is irreversible toward the methylated sterol (zymosterol -> fecosterol, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' is not an enzymatically accessible direction.

enzyme_name: UDP-N-acetylgalactosamine-4-sulfate 6-O-sulfotransferase (microsomal avian oviduct activity; protein never purified or cloned)
organism_context: Quail/hen oviduct tubular gland microsomes
rationale: The only characterisation of EC 2.8.2.7 is a microsomal 'sulfotransferase-sulfatase' multienzyme system in quail oviduct, in which a PAPS-dependent 6-O-sulfotransferase makes UDP-GalNAc 4,6-bissulfate and a physically separate 4-sulfatase then removes the 4-sulfate; the sulfotransferase itself was never purified, so its domain organisation and even its identity are unknown.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfonation is essentially irreversible toward the sulfated sugar nucleotide (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would regenerate PAPS from a sulfate ester, which no sulfotransferase does, so the LLM's '>' is the defensible call even though the protein is unidentified.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous ring-chain (hemiketal) tautomerisation; the EC 5.5.1.1 tag in ModelSEED is a mis-assignment
organism_context: Protocatechuate 4,5-cleavage (meta) pathway of Sphingomonas/Pseudomonas
rationale: KEGG R04489 carries no EC and no KO and is annotated 'tautomeric equilibrium': the interconversion of 4-carboxy-2-hydroxymuconate-6-semialdehyde with its intramolecular hemiketal (2-hydroxy-2-hydropyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate) is spontaneous, and the enzymatic step in this pathway is the downstream LigC dehydrogenase acting on the cyclic form. EC 5.5.1.1 is muconate cycloisomerase and does not belong to this chemistry.
direction_note: The equilibrium lies on the cyclic hemiketal side and pathway flux runs semialdehyde -> hemiketal -> (LigC) 2-pyrone-4,6-dicarboxylate, i.e. right-to-left as the ModelSEED equation is written; here ModelSEED's '<' is the correct direction and the LLM's '>' is not, consistent with eQuilibrator's +21 kJ/mol for the left-to-right (decyclizing) sense.

organism_context: Escherichia coli ThiD, a single gene that complements both thiJ and thiD mutations; the yeast orthologues THI20/THI21 add a third, TenA-type aminopyrimidine aminohydrolase (thiaminase II) activity and are effectively polyfunctional
rationale: A single purified E. coli ThiD polypeptide converts HMP to its monophosphate and the monophosphate to its pyrophosphate, so two distinct kinase activities sit on one chain; in Saccharomyces the same protein family carries an additional hydrolase domain.
direction_note: This ATP-dependent second phosphorylation is the committed step supplying HMP-PP to thiamine phosphate synthase, and the enzyme's other (HMP kinase) activity pushes flux the same way, so the biosynthetic/salvage direction is left-to-right as written and ModelSEED's '<' reverses it; the bifunctionality here reinforces rather than explains the conflict.

organism_context: Human liver and kidney peroxisomes (rat has a distinct trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase alongside pristanoyl-CoA oxidase)
rationale: The human peroxisomal branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase was purified to near homogeneity as a single ~70 kDa monomeric protein with one activity, FAD-dependent alpha,beta-desaturation, acting on both 3alpha,7alpha-dihydroxy- and 3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoyl-CoA; the following hydratase and dehydrogenase steps live on a separate multifunctional protein (MFP-2), not on the oxidase.
direction_note: The physiological enzyme is an O2-dependent oxidase that dumps the electrons as H2O2, making the desaturation irreversible left-to-right as written; ModelSEED's FAD/FADH2 formulation hides that irreversibility and its '<' call would reduce the 24-ene back, which peroxisomal bile-acid synthesis never does.

organism_context: Human liver and kidney peroxisomes; in rat liver a separate trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase performs the same step
rationale: The same single ~70 kDa monomeric human branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase oxidises 3alpha,7alpha,12alpha-trihydroxy-5beta-cholestanoyl-CoA (THCA-CoA) as well as 2-methyl-branched acyl-CoAs; it has one catalytic activity and no fused hydratase/dehydrogenase domains.
direction_note: As an O2-consuming, H2O2-producing acyl-CoA oxidase the step is irreversible toward the 24-enoyl-CoA (left-to-right as written) on the way to cholic acid; ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of writing the half-reaction with FAD/FADH2 instead of O2/H2O2.

enzyme_name: Stizolobate synthase (L-DOPA 4,5-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.29) - catalysing protein never isolated
organism_context: Etiolated Stizolobium hassjoo (Mucuna) seedlings
rationale: The only enzymology is a crude, oxygen-labile ammonium-sulfate fraction from Stizolobium hassjoo seedlings that converts L-DOPA to stizolobic acid in the presence of O2 and NAD(P)+; Saito and Komamine themselves speak of 'an enzyme system(s)', KEGG notes R04598 is 'possibly a two-step reaction', and no protein has been purified or cloned, so mono- versus bifunctionality cannot be judged.
direction_note: The biosynthesis requires NAD(P)+ as oxidant, i.e. the ring-opened muconate semialdehyde + NAD+ -> stizolobate + NADH (left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' runs the plant biosynthetic step backwards and the LLM's '>' matches the only experimental evidence.

enzyme_name: Stizolobinate synthase (L-DOPA 2,3-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.30) - catalysing protein never isolated
organism_context: Etiolated Stizolobium hassjoo (Mucuna) seedlings
rationale: Same crude preparation as for stizolobic acid: a single partially purified, oxygen-labile Stizolobium hassjoo fraction makes both stizolobinic and stizolobic acid from L-DOPA with O2 and NAD(P)+, and it was never resolved into individual proteins, so whether one, two or more polypeptides are involved is unresolved.
direction_note: NAD(P)+ is the oxidant in the demonstrated biosynthesis (semialdehyde + NAD+ -> stizolobinate + NADH, left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' reverses the only direction the cell-free system was shown to run.

organism_context: Escherichia coli FolE homodecamer; human GCH1 (folate and tetrahydrobiopterin biosynthesis)
rationale: This ModelSEED entry is the final cyclization partial-step of GTP cyclohydrolase I; the E. coli enzyme is a homodecamer whose single active site, formed at subunit interfaces, carries out the whole GTP -> dihydroneopterin triphosphate conversion (imidazole ring opening, formate release, Amadori rearrangement, pterin ring closure) as one catalytic activity, not several fused ones. A literature search for a bifunctional GTP cyclohydrolase I returned nothing.
direction_note: Folate/pterin biosynthetic flux runs from the open formamidopyrimidine intermediate to 7,8-dihydroneopterin 3'-triphosphate with loss of water, i.e. right-to-left as this equation is written; here ModelSEED's '<' agrees with the enzyme and the LLM's '>' (hydrolytic re-opening of the pterin ring) does not.

enzyme_name: none - a lumped multi-enzyme sterol C-4 demethylation plus Delta24 reduction, not a single enzyme
organism_context: Fungal (ERG25/ERG26/ERG27/ERG4) and mammalian (SC4MOL/MSMO1, NSDHL, HSD17B7, DHCR24) post-squalene sterol pathways
rationale: No single protein converts 14-demethyllanosterol to 4alpha-methylcholest-8-en-3beta-ol: removing one C-4 methyl requires the three sequential, separately encoded C-4 demethylation enzymes (sterol C4-methyl oxidase, C-3 sterol dehydrogenase/C-4 decarboxylase, 3-ketosteroid reductase) and the Delta24 bond must additionally be reduced by a sterol Delta24-reductase; the entry is also not mass-balanced as written (a carbon is lost with no CO2 product).
direction_note: Sterol biosynthesis runs in the demethylating sense (14-demethyllanosterol -> 4alpha-methyl sterol, left-to-right as written) and every component step is irreversible (O2- and NAD(P)H-consuming, CO2-releasing), so ModelSEED's '<' is unachievable; but because the entry lumps several enzymes and is unbalanced, no direction call on it is really meaningful.

organism_context: Coptis japonica, Papaver somniferum, Thalictrum flavum (benzylisoquinoline alkaloid biosynthesis)
rationale: The CNMT crystal structure shows a single class-I SAM-binding methyltransferase domain with one active site that N-methylates (S)-coclaurine and related 1-benzyltetrahydroisoquinolines; its broad substrate scope is promiscuity at that one site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH N-methylation is effectively irreversible toward (S)-N-methylcoclaurine (left-to-right as written) and is a committed step toward reticuline, so ModelSEED's '<' is not an enzymatic direction.

organism_context: Coptis japonica / Papaver somniferum CNMT and its paralogues; EC 2.1.1.115 activity measured on generic 1-benzyl-THIQ substrates
rationale: EC 2.1.1.115 on an unspecified 1-benzyltetrahydroisoquinoline is the same CNMT-family class-I SAM methyltransferase characterised structurally for coclaurine, a single-domain enzyme with one N-methylation activity and broad acceptor tolerance; medium confidence because the ModelSEED substrate is generic rather than a named natural product.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible toward the N-methylated alkaloid (left-to-right as written), so ModelSEED's '<' does not correspond to any methyltransferase chemistry.

organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria (pig/human MCAD homotetramer); hexanoyl-CoA is a core MCAD substrate, with short-chain ACADS overlapping at C6
rationale: MCAD is a homotetrameric FAD enzyme whose crystal structures show one catalytic site per identical subunit performing a single alpha,beta-dehydrogenation; the electron-transfer flavoprotein that reoxidises it is a separate protein, which the protocol's complex exclusion keeps out of the bifunctional category.
direction_note: beta-Oxidation dehydrogenation is pulled by ETF/ETF-QO and runs only toward the 2-enoyl-CoA (hexanoyl-CoA -> (2E)-hexenoyl-CoA, left-to-right as written); the reverse reduction is done by a different enzyme (trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase in fatty-acid elongation), so ModelSEED's '<' misassigns the chemistry.

enzyme_name: Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD, ACADM; long-chain ACADL/ACADVL overlap at C10)
organism_context: Mammalian mitochondria; decanoyl-CoA sits at the MCAD/LCAD chain-length boundary
rationale: Decanoyl-CoA dehydrogenation is carried out by homotetrameric ACAD-family flavoenzymes (MCAD, with LCAD/VLCAD overlapping at C10), each a single-activity dehydrogenase with one catalytic site per subunit and no fused second domain.
direction_note: As with all ACADs the step is drained to ETF and is physiologically unidirectional toward (2E)-decenoyl-CoA (left-to-right as written); ModelSEED's '<' would be an enoyl-CoA reductase activity that this enzyme does not have.

enzyme_name: L-Methionine gamma-lyase (methioninase, MGL); the co-listed EC 4.4.1.1 points instead to cystathionine gamma-lyase
organism_context: Pseudomonas putida and Trichomonas vaginalis MGL; in mouse liver the alpha,gamma-elimination of selenomethionine is attributed to cystathionine gamma-lyase
rationale: MGL is a homotetrameric PLP enzyme with one active site; its alpha,gamma-elimination, gamma-replacement and beta-elimination/replacement reactions are all variants of the same PLP chemistry at that single site, i.e. catalytic promiscuity rather than two fused catalytic domains. The same applies to cystathionine gamma-lyase.
direction_note: Selenomethionine is an even better alpha,gamma-elimination substrate than methionine and the products include volatile methaneselenol, making the reaction effectively irreversible left-to-right as written; MGL's gamma-replacement chemistry can insert selenols into homocysteine derivatives but does not reassemble selenomethionine from 2-oxobutyrate + NH3, so ModelSEED's '<' has no enzymatic basis.
